title: Statistics on Employment of Persons with Disabilities
what_it_is: Statistics on Employment of Persons with Disabilities

sections.label: PwD resident employment rate
sections.summary: The resident employment rate among persons with disabilities aged 15 to 64 was 28.6%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Among PwDs in the working ages of 15 to 64, the resident employment rate was 28.6%.

sections.label: PwD employment rates by age
sections.summary: Resident employment rates for PwDs were 27.6% for ages 15 to 39, 37.8% for 40 to 49, 26.1% for 50 to 64, and 5.9% for 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The resident employment rates for PwDs were 27.6% for those aged 15 and 39; 37.8% for those aged between 40 and 49; 26.1% for those aged between 50 and 64; and 5.9% for those aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Employers benefiting from SEC
sections.summary: Last year, more than 5,700 employers hiring over 8,600 Singaporeans with disabilities benefited from SEC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Last year, more than 5,700 employers hiring over 8,600 Singaporeans with disabilities benefited from SEC.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow PwD hiring
sections.summary: From January 2016 to June this year, close to 780 companies hired more than 2,000 PwDs with Adapt and Grow support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: From January 2016 to June this year, close to 780 companies have hired more than 2,000 PwDs with support from the Adapt and Grow initiative.

sections.label: Difference from newspaper figures
sections.summary: The Minister of State was asked to explain the difference between his cited numbers and newspaper figures, which he said were erroneous.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Could the Minister of State please shed some light on the difference in the numbers that he has just cited versus what was reported in the newspapers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I have said that today's employment rate for those between the ages of 15 and 64 was 28.6%, which is different from the 5% that was cited by The Straits Times in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: This was erroneous because the incorrect data was derived by The Straits Times using different sources of publicly available data.

sections.label: Straits Times employed PwD data
sections.summary: The Straits Times used an MSF Parliamentary Question reply figure combining private sector PwDs eligible for SEC and Public Service PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: For example, for the number of employed PwDs, The Straits Times had used the number reported by MSF in a Parliamentary Question reply which is a composite of PwDs in the private sector who are eligible for the SEC, as well as PwDs in the Public Service.

sections.label: National target for PwD employment
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there are plans to commit to a national target, noting at least 60% of PwDs from Adapt and Grow stayed employed after six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second question is, do we have any plans to commit to a national target?

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Earlier, I mentioned that for those PwDs who came through our Adapt and Grow initiatives, at least 60% remained employed after six months.

sections.label: No national target yet
sections.summary: A national target has been considered but is not being committed to now; the focus is improving employment rates by getting more employers on board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Overall, in terms of a national target, it is something we have considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: But I do not think we are prepared to do it at this point, given that we have just got some good visibility on how the situation is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: I think our commitment for now is that our employment rates can be improved and this is something for which we need to get more employers on board in order to improve the employment rate and placements for our PwDs.
